question: Should ClawHub adopt `claimState`, `officialState`, and `restrictionState` as an admin-client contract once claim derivation requires an observed active account?
rationale: These names and derivation rules become identity and trust signals that downstream tooling can treat as authoritative; code review cannot determine the intended permanent product contract.

options.title: Approve after correction and proof
options.body: Keep the three-axis contract, require fail-closed active-account derivation, and require redacted real Convex/API proof before merge.

options.title: Land the specification only
options.body: Retain the durable state-boundary design record but remove the runtime response and client-schema additions until the API contract is sponsored.

options.title: Defer the state contract
options.body: Pause or close the runtime feature if maintainers do not want these identity-state concepts exposed to admin clients yet.

recommendation.title: Approve after correction and proof
recommendation.body: Keep the three-axis contract, require fail-closed active-account derivation, and require redacted real Convex/API proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is the requested code owner and has the strongest recent history on the exact official-publisher admin and client-schema surfaces.
